answer: Require every agent identity to be backed by a locked, slashable bond tied to a single attested execution kernel: the agent must periodically prove it still runs that exact kernel and has completed useful work, and misbehaviour burns the bond. A raven-like swarm of fake identities then stops being cheap, because each copy needs its own bond and its own proven history. At the nadir of trust, when a new identity has no record, it earns only tiny, rate-limited tasks until its bond and history grow, so creating thousands of sock puppets costs far more than any reward they could steal.
